subject.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying

question: Should model-boundary interception use new opt-in modifier hooks, or should the shipped `llm_input` and `llm_output` observation hooks be converted in place across every agent backend?
rationale: The choice changes a public plugin contract and grants installed plugins new security- and availability-sensitive authority over every model call; patch correctness alone cannot determine the permanent API direction.

options.title: Add separate modifier hooks
options.body: Preserve the observation hooks and introduce new explicitly modifying hooks with a documented backend support and permission contract.

options.title: Convert every backend uniformly
options.body: Change the existing names only after all runners, documentation, compatibility tests, and upgrade behavior implement identical semantics.

options.title: Keep observation only
options.body: Decline synchronous installed-plugin control of model requests and responses.

recommendation.title: Add separate modifier hooks
recommendation.body: Preserve the observation hooks and introduce new explicitly modifying hooks with a documented backend support and permission contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the shipped hook contract and are the strongest available feature-history owner for this API decision.
